title: Anthropic's new budget model gets much better at ignoring hidden commands
source_used: Help Net Security (fulltext, read in full)
key_facts: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5, its model for quick, repetitive and speed-sensitive tasks, is better than Haiku 4.5 at finding vulnerabilities and writing exploits, and has stricter cyber safeguards than Haiku 4.5 but lighter than its more advanced models.

With safeguards off, in a test of known flaws in Chrome's V8 engine it achieved arbitrary code execution in four of 410 runs; a pre-release version completed 3.3% of multi-stage cyber challenges against 46.1% for Sonnet 5.5 and 67.6% for Opus 5.5.
In Claude Code tests it refused 84.3% of malicious requests, up from 66.6% for Haiku 4.5; in computer-use tests about 82.6%, up from 58.9%.
It gave harmless responses to 99.71% of harmful requests and wrongly refused 0.82% of harmless ones, down from 3.05% for Haiku 4.5.

Anthropic calls it its most prompt-injection-resistant Haiku; against adaptive attackers it largely matched the frontier models, but was less resistant than Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 on a separate Gray Swan benchmark, mostly in graphical computer use.
Most tests excluded additional production safeguards; Anthropic advises API developers to add their own safeguards.
Token prices are 90% lower than Haiku 4.5 for prompts up to 100,000 tokens.
quote_evidence: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 is its most resistant Haiku model yet to prompt injection.
In Claude Code tests, the model refused 84.3% of malicious requests, up from 66.6% for Haiku 4.5.
Most of these tests excluded additional production safeguards.
why_it_matters_hint: A cheap, fast model that is harder to trick with hidden instructions matters because it will run inside many automated agents, but the numbers are Anthropic's own.
notes: All figures are Anthropic's own evaluations as reported by Help Net Security; Anthropic's system card was not opened.
